brain oscillatory dynamics in major depressive disorder are characterized by a network dysfunction in which a relative decrease in the amplitude of the alpha band and a relative increase in the beta band are associated with a decrease in functional connectivity in the default mode network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a complex dynamical system and the brain rhythms and oscillations are the signatures of this dynamical system.
the use of multiple encephalogram modalities can provide complementary information to better understand network dysfunctions that may be associated with depression.
